title: The Pell Regulator Scales Linearly Along All Integer Powers (zpow Extension)
description: Answers the parent entry's first open question: extends the regulator scaling law from non-negative to all integer exponents. Because Mathlib's Pell solutions Solution₁ d form a group (the inverse of (x,y) is the conjugate (x,−y)), a solution can be raised to any integer power. The Pell norm x + y√d intertwines the group's integer-power operation with real zpow — pellNorm(aⁿ) = (pellNorm a)ⁿ for every n ∈ ℤ — so the regulator log(x+y√d) is a genuine ℤ-linear function of the exponent: pellRegulator(aⁿ) = n·pellRegulator(a) for all n ∈ ℤ, negatives included. The seed is pellNorm(a⁻¹) = (pellNorm a)⁻¹ (the conjugate identity as reciprocation); the engine is an integer induction matched on the real side by zpow_add_one₀ / zpow_sub_one₀, and Real.log_zpow finishes the regulator law. 9 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The solutions of Pell's equation x² − d·y² = 1 (for non-square d > 0) form an infinite group, generated up to sign by a fundamental solution; the embedding (x, y) ↦ x + y√d sends it into the units of the real quadratic order ℤ[√d], and the logarithm of that embedding is the regulator. The grandparent entry pell-equation-oq-01-oq-04 proved the Pell norm is multiplicative (Brahmagupta) and the regulator additive, but established the linear scaling law R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) only for n ∈ ℕ. Yet the solution group has inverses — the conjugate (x, −y) — so it is natural to raise a solution to a negative power, and the scaling law should persist over all of ℤ. This entry closes that gap, completing the picture of the regulator as a ℤ-linear invariant.
overview.problemStatement: Extend the regulator scaling law from non-negative to all integer exponents: show pellNorm(aⁿ) = (pellNorm a)ⁿ and pellRegulator(aⁿ) = n·pellRegulator(a) for every n ∈ ℤ, where the negative powers use the Pell group's inverse (the conjugate solution).
overview.proofStrategy: Work over Mathlib's Solution₁ d with pellNorm d x y = x + y√d. The new seed is pellNorm_inv: pellNorm(a⁻¹) = (pellNorm a)⁻¹, obtained from the parent's conjugate identity pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(a⁻¹) = 1 together with non-vanishing of the norm. The main law pellNorm_zpow is proved by Int.induction_on: the base case is pellNorm(a⁰) = 1; the forward step rewrites a^(n+1) = aⁿ·a (group zpow_add_one), applies pellNorm_mul, and matches the real side with zpow_add_one₀; the backward step rewrites a^(n−1) = aⁿ·a⁻¹ (zpow_sub_one), applies pellNorm_mul and pellNorm_inv, and matches the real side with zpow_sub_one₀. The regulator law pellRegulator_zpow is then log of pellNorm_zpow via Real.log_zpow, and the negative-exponent corollaries (R(a⁻¹) = −R(a), R(a⁻ⁿ) = −n·R(a)) are instances.
keyInsights: **The conjugate identity becomes reciprocation.** The parent's pellNorm(a)·pellNorm(a⁻¹) = 1, together with pellNorm ≠ 0, forces pellNorm(a⁻¹) = (pellNorm a)⁻¹. This single fact is what lets the inductive scaling law cross from the positive into the negative half of the exponent line.

**Integer induction, not natural-number induction.** Int.induction_on supplies a forward step (n → n+1) and a backward step (−n → −n−1) around the base 0. The forward step reuses the parent's natural-number argument; the backward step is its mirror image with a⁻¹ in place of a — the only genuinely new computation.

**The group's zpow and the field's zpow line up term by term.** zpow_add_one / zpow_sub_one on the Pell solution group and zpow_add_one₀ / zpow_sub_one₀ on ℝ have identical shapes, so multiplicativity (pellNorm_mul) transfers each inductive step from the group to the reals with no arithmetic left over.

**The regulator is genuinely ℤ-linear.** R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for all n ∈ ℤ means the regulator is an honest group homomorphism (Solution₁ d, ·) → (ℝ, +) restricted to a cyclic subgroup; the image of R on ⟨a⟩ is the full subgroup R(a)·ℤ of (ℝ, +), not merely the non-negative spacing R(a)·ℕ the parent exhibited.
**Only d ≥ 0 is used.** As in the parent, the lone analytic ingredient is (√d)² = d; the entire extension to ℤ is group theory plus the real zpow algebra, so it holds for every non-negative d.

sections.title: Norm of the inverse is the reciprocal
sections.summary: pellNorm_inv: pellNorm(a⁻¹) = (pellNorm a)⁻¹, derived from the conjugate identity and non-vanishing. The new seed that opens the negative half of the exponent line.

sections.title: The norm intertwines integer powers with real zpow
sections.summary: pellNorm_zpow: pellNorm(aⁿ) = (pellNorm a)ⁿ for every n ∈ ℤ, by Int.induction_on — forward step via zpow_add_one₀, backward step via pellNorm_inv and zpow_sub_one₀.

sections.title: The regulator is ℤ-linear in the exponent
sections.summary: pellRegulator_zpow: R(aⁿ) = n·R(a) for all n ∈ ℤ (Real.log_zpow), with corollaries pellRegulator_inv (R(a⁻¹) = −R(a)) and pellRegulator_zpow_neg (R(a⁻ⁿ) = −n·R(a)).

conclusion.summary: The Pell norm x + y√d intertwines the solution group's integer-power operation with real zpow — pellNorm(aⁿ) = (pellNorm a)ⁿ for all n ∈ ℤ — so the regulator scales linearly along every integer power, R(aⁿ) = n·R(a), negatives included. This closes the parent entry's first open question. 9 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Completes the structural description of the Pell regulator: it is a genuine homomorphism (Solution₁ d, ·) → (ℝ, +) whose restriction to the cyclic subgroup generated by a solution a has image exactly R(a)·ℤ. The negative-exponent corollary R(a⁻¹) = −R(a) makes precise that conjugation negates the regulator, the analytic shadow of inversion in the unit group.
openQuestions: Package pellNorm as an actual MonoidHom Solution₁ d →* ℝˣ and pellRegulator as an AddMonoidHom Solution₁ d →+ ℝ, then derive pellNorm_zpow / pellRegulator_zpow as instances of map_zpow.

Combine with Mathlib's IsFundamental to identify R(fundamental) as the positive generator of the regulator subgroup R(a)·ℤ, characterizing the regulator as the minimal positive value over all solutions.
